title: Static Data Members and Static Methods
learningObjectives: Explain static data members and static methods.
Identify relevant class/object relationships and access rules.
Apply the OOP concept in a small design.

understand.concept: Static data members belong to the class rather than each instance. Static member functions can be called without an object and cannot access non-static members directly.
understand.whyItMatters: Shared counters, configuration and class-wide utilities may be appropriate static members.
understand.explain: Distinguish per-object state from class-wide state and initialize static members correctly.

examples.title: Shared counter
examples.code: class Ticket{public:Ticket(){++created;}static int count(){return created;}private:static int created;};\nint Ticket::created=0;
examples.explanation: Static data member is shared across all Ticket objects.

examples.title: Class utility
examples.code: class Convert{public:static int toInt(char c){return c-'0';}};\nint n=Convert::toInt('7');
examples.explanation: Static method can be called through class name.

examples.title: Static and instance
examples.code: class Example{public:static int shared;int local=0;};\nint Example::shared=5;
examples.explanation: shared belongs to class; local belongs to each object.

examples.title: Update shared state
examples.code: class Counter{public:static void reset(){total=0;}static int total;};\nint Counter::total=0;
examples.explanation: Static method can update static member.

examples.title: Access static data
examples.code: class Settings{public:static int limit;};\nint Settings::limit=10;\nint max=Settings::limit;
examples.explanation: Access class-wide data through the class name.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze the five Static Data Members and Static Methods examples. Identify class responsibilities, interface, object state, lifetime and dispatch behavior where relevant.
practise.independentTask: Design a small C++ program demonstrating static data members and static methods in a practical domain. Use clear public operations, appropriate access control, and tests for expected behavior and edge cases.
hints: Start by listing responsibilities and objects.
Keep internal state protected where needed.
Initialize objects deliberately and understand lifetime.
Use inheritance only for substitutable relationships.
Test behavior through the public interface.

questions.prompt: Static method can access non-static member directly?
questions.explanation: No instance exists for the static function.
Each instance has its own ordinary data member.
Static state can count class-wide instances.
